answer: Admission requires an unaffiliated underwriter to post a bond vouching for a new agent. Each underwriter can back only a handful of peers at its zenith of capacity, so every extra clone a farm spins up demands a fresh outside sponsor it cannot manufacture. If the sworn independence claim later proves false, the posted bond is burned. Honest backers are as rare as a comet, and a borrowed one leaves its sponsor on a ledge of slashable collateral, so N aliases cost N real sponsors and the price cannot be pooled across cooperating operators.
